decisions.rationale: Add the real-machine install path per OS with numbered steps and java/javac/mvn verification; keep PATH repair as troubleshooting.
Complete mkdir/tar -xzf -C/PATH commands for macOS and Linux.
Use Fedora/RHEL-documented `sudo alternatives --config java|javac`; keep update-alternatives for Debian/Ubuntu only. Confirmed resolved by the final education recheck.
Label reads 'About 15 minutes, plus your download and install time'; estimator worst path 14.98 within the 15 ceiling. Confirmed resolved.
Replace blanket 'answer y' with the two expected prompts (package confirmation, Adoptium key import) and 'stop and ask for help' otherwise. Confirmed resolved.

Restore the Linux Maven expect/done cue ('Expect no output; it is done when the prompt returns with no error.'); headroom created by trimming three non-step intro/recap phrases only, per captain decision. Final education recheck confirms no step cue or needed teaching point was lost.
Same Linux Maven expect/done cue as java-basics-edu-recheck-005; final SME recheck confirms resolved and technically accurate.

[2026-11-10 DESIGN.md re-authoring round; decided by independent non-author reconciler, fresh Claude subagent (Claude Opus 5.5); did not author the page or either critic report] Accept; partly fixed, still open at low impact, does not block release (medium at filing, now Windows-only). Fixed: step 3 has a completion check ("Done when mvn -v prints a Maven version in the next step") and the cheat-sheet note now says only the Temurin installer sets PATH and JAVA_HOME and the learner adds Maven bin to Path. Remaining: a Windows learner gets no route for editing Path and no early stop-and-ask; the troubleshooting line "repeat the guide's PATH step" points to a Maven guide step with no Windows detail. Reproducing OS Path-editing steps is excluded by the product decision, so the minimal fix (recommended in the next correction loop on this module branch, before release if one is run) is one sentence in step 3: "On Windows, if you have not edited Path before, ask your instructor before you continue." The existing general stop-and-ask boundary already catches learners after a failed check.
